findings.summary: In the migrate-loop's default (failure) case branch, the `failed=$((failed + 1))` increment present in the old code was dropped when the case body was rewritten. Now any non-201/409 migrate outcome (real HTTP error OR a network failure that leaves status empty) prints a FAILED line but never increments `failed`. The final summary `failed=${failed}` under-reports, and the exit gate `[[ "$failed" -eq 0 ]] || exit 1` no longer fires for migrate failures — the nightly cron job exits 0 (success) even when repos failed to mirror. This directly undermines the brief's goal of letting callers 'reliably branch on status codes... across the enumeration and migration loops', since the branch exists but its bookkeeping is broken.

findings.summary: gh_api()'s curl call has no --max-time at all, while gitea_api() got --max-time 60/1800 added specifically to satisfy 'bound how long any single request can run'. The brief names both gh_api and gitea_api as the helpers to rework, and the timeout requirement isn't scoped to only one of them. A stalled TCP connection to api.github.com during the paginated enumeration loop can now hang the entire script indefinitely, which is exactly the failure mode the rest of this change is meant to guard against.

findings.summary: body_msg() always reads whatever is currently in $BODY_FILE. If curl fails before it opens/truncates the output file (e.g. a DNS failure or connection refusal prior to any data), $BODY_FILE still holds the body from the previous successful call, so die()/the FAILED log line can print a stale, unrelated error message instead of an empty one. Narrow edge case, but it can mislead whoever is debugging a real network failure in this now-more-resilient path.
